what_it_does: SRAM (the fastest on-chip memory in processors) must operate at a minimum voltage to stay stable during reads and writes, but other parts of a modern chip run at lower voltages to save power. This creates a problem: level-shifter circuits are needed to translate signals between different voltage domains, but they waste area and power. This paper presents a new SRAM design (using the latest 3-nanometer finFET technology) where the memory cells themselves run at low voltage (380 millivolts) through an extended-range level shifter that operates at the chip's standard voltage. This decoupling lets the rest of the chip run optimally while SRAM achieves record-breaking density of 38 megabits per square millimeter.
